$comment: THE CODEMIE PROVIDER SET — which models this stack runs, and what each is allowed to spend. Set-INDEPENDENT budgets (effortTiers, roleOverrides, outputTokenFloors) stay in llm-defaults.json and are shared by every set, so swapping providers never changes how much budget a TIER gets — only which models serve it.
$measured: Every model value here was MEASURED against the live CodeMie proxy on 2026-08-25, not taken from documentation: contextWindow and maxOutputTokens come from the probe's own modelUsage block. sonnet-4-6 reported 32000 max output; sonnet-5, opus-4-8 and opus-5 all reported 64000. claude-sonnet-4-6 was DROPPED for that reason — half the output ceiling at a slightly higher per-token cost makes it strictly dominated by sonnet-5.

medium.$why: Enters cheap and tops out at Sonnet-5. A `mid` seam never reaches Opus: 14 seams resolve here, and measured turn counts are p50 4, p90 24 — work that does not need a frontier model.

high.$why: Same ENTRY as medium, higher CEILING. That is the 'different entry, same ceiling' rule applied between high and highest: what separates the tiers is how far they may climb, not where they start.

highest.$why: Skips Haiku. 25 seams resolve here and would waste a rung proving a small model cannot do the work. Same ceiling as high, entered two rungs up.

modelOverrides.$whyAutoCompress: 150000 against a 200000 window is an OVERFLOW GUARD near the ceiling, never a token-saving device: compaction rewrites the prefix and destroys the prompt cache. Measured input is p50 13.3k, p90 19k, max 25.9k — about 13% of the window — so this should never fire. If it does, something has gone wrong upstream and that is worth knowing.
modelOverrides.$whyNoTemperature: codemie-claude exposes no temperature flag and Claude Code has no supported lever for it. Declaring one would be decoration. Deliberation is controlled by reasoningEffort and thinking instead.
modelOverrides.$whyAdaptive: Thinking is held STABLE per model. Anthropic's docs list effort and thinking-parameter changes as cache invalidators, so a config that changes between attempts discards the cache every retry — the opposite of what a 1h TTL is for.
modelOverrides.$miniTierWhy: miniTier marks the cheap, fast rung — the models that are quick but limited in generation capacity. It was decided in engine code by sniffing vendor naming habits (-mini, -flash, -haiku, minimax-m2), which breaks in both directions: a cheap model named differently read as capable, and a capable model containing -flash read as cheap. The set that declares the model declares its tier.
modelOverrides.$whyCharsPerToken: INPUT CAPACITY IN CHARACTERS. autoCompressAt is the models input ceiling in TOKENS; callers that must size a payload measure it in characters. The ratio belongs with the model, because it is a property of that models tokenizer, not of any caller. Declared so a caller derives its budget instead of inventing one: the roster review carried a literal 60000 in code, which split a 276KB roster into six calls and failed the whole review whenever any one of them answered off-schema.

finalFallback.$why: Applies after ladder exhaustion — the one point where the ladder has nothing left to say. Sonnet-5 differs from the top rung on high and highest, so it is a real second answer rather than a retry of the model that just failed.

codemie-claude.$whyAlwaysFlags: -s is a CORRECTNESS requirement, not a preference. Without it the wrapper opens an INTERACTIVE menu about the Claude Code version gap and exits 13 — in a pipeline that is a HANG, not a failure: the run waits for a keypress until its timeout.
codemie-claude.$whyNoBaseUrl: --base-url is deliberately absent. It selects an SSO PROFILE rather than redirecting: pointing it elsewhere fails with 'SSO credentials not found'. Declaring it would break the run, not redirect it.
codemie-claude.$whyNoTimeoutFlag: No --timeout mapping. The wall is ALREADY enforced as a command prefix around the wrapper (claude.sh: `timeout $EPAM_STORY_TIMEOUT_SECS codemie-claude ...`), and it is DERIVED from the attempt's own iteration budget rather than fixed — a fixed wall once SIGKILLed 10 of 23 invocations mid-flight, the most expensive attempts of that run. Passing a second timeout would raise the question of which wins and which an operator reads. One wall.
codemie-claude.$whyFlags: Checked against the installed CLI's own --help, not assumed: --effort takes (low, medium, high, xhigh, max) and --autocompact takes auto or a token count. These were declared as CLAUDE_CODE_* env vars that the CLI does not document and that nothing exported.
codemie-claude.$whyNoTurnCap: maxIterations is deliberately absent. It binds the ReAct loop in src/agent/AgentRunner.ts, which only the `epam run` arm enters; a --print call has no turn cap and the loop is Claude Code's own. Declaring one here would name a knob nothing can turn.
codemie-claude.$whyNoOutputCap: maxOutputTokens is deliberately unmapped: the installed CLI documents no flag or env for it. It stays declared in modelOverrides so the intent is visible, and is not routed anywhere pretending to work.
codemie-claude.$emitsTraces: Whether model calls made through this runner reach Langfuse. TRUE for every runner: traces are emitted by lib/cost-emitter.js at the cost seam — the point every arm passes through with its model, tokens, cost and timing resolved — not by the TypeScript provider decorator, which only the epam arm reaches. Verified end-to-end 2026-09-04 by driving the real emitter and reading the session back out of Langfuse.
